Diagram pipeline · 8 September 2026

GPT-Image-2.5 against the canary

OpenAI shipped 2.5 Flare and 2.5 Sunburst this morning at the same token prices as GPT-Image-2. This sheet re-runs the two canary units through Flare with the prompt template untouched, tries two alternative house styles against the one running today, and tests whether reference images can lock a style across subjects on Sunburst. Every picture was judged by the vision gate in the context of its lesson — and the 4 September images were re-judged by the same gate today, so the accept rates below compare models rather than moods.

343output tokens per Flare image, against 1,372 on GPT-Image-2
1.0pper image, all in, at $30/M out and $5/M text in
3/18accepted first attempt, against 2/18 for GPT-Image-2
£0.44spent on all 40 images in this round
01

What it costs and what survives the gate

One attempt per brief, no retries, both models on the same 18 briefs, both judged today by the same gate under the same rubric. “One correction” is the gate’s retry verdict: the picture is worth another go with a named fix. The pipeline budgets one retry in three and bins on a second reject.

ModelAcceptedOne correctionBinned Tokens outPer imagePer accepted imageSeconds
GPT-Image-2  4 Sep 2/18133 1,3723.38p 30p~46
2.5 Flare  8 Sep 3/18141 3430.96p 6p~15
Change+1 +1-2 −75%−72% −81% 3× faster

Read the accept column carefully. Today’s gate is a harder marker than the one that ran on 4–5 September: it crops in on every leader line and counts a line that lands on the neighbouring organelle as a fault, which the earlier pass let through. That is why both models score lower here than the canary reported at the time, and it is exactly why the old images were re-judged today rather than compared on their old verdicts. The column that matters is the difference between the two rows, not the absolute rate.

Fleet arithmetic, on cost rather than on this one-attempt accept rate: at 0.96p a render and the canary’s measured 1.45 renders per briefed lesson, one visual for each of about 3,500 free-tier lessons is roughly £49 of generation, against £172 at GPT-Image-2 prices. Unity’s 552 article lessons come to about £8. Both figures halve again if the 2.5 models reach the Batch allow-list.

Batch

The Batch endpoint takes images, but not these models yet. The docs list /v1/images/generations and /v1/images/edits among the batchable endpoints at the usual 50% discount and a 24-hour window, and a batch created with gpt-image-2 validated and started running. The same batch body with gpt-image-2.5-flare or gpt-image-2.5-sunburst fails at validation: “is not supported by the Batch API”.

So this round ran synchronously at full price, and the figures above are undiscounted. When the 2.5 models reach the Batch allow-list, halve them again. Flare is fast enough — about fifteen seconds an image, five at a time — that a fleet run does not need the 24-hour window to be practical.

03

Three house styles, one brief at a time

Six briefs spanning the visual forms — two labelled diagrams, a data picture, a scene, a sequence and a map — each rendered three times on Flare. Only the style block changes; the brief text, the labels, the facts and the accent are identical across the three. A is the block running today. B asks for ink line work with loose watercolour fills, to sit with the painted book spines on the shelf. C asks for flat geometric shapes with no outlines and a palette of four colours.

Style blockAcceptedOne correction What it does when it goes wrong
A  Textbook2/6 4Leader lines land on the neighbouring structure; annotation prose creeps in beside the drawing.
B  Line-and-wash2/6 4Decorates: period vignettes bolted onto a bar chart, washes soft enough to blur cell boundaries.
C  Flat isotype1/6 5Reaches for faceless silhouettes, and flattens away the distinctions the label list exists to make.

04

Can three references carry a house style?

These three Flare images went to Sunburst as style references on the image-edit path, with four brand-new briefs from chemistry, geography, physics and computer science that share none of their content. No style block was sent in words: the references had to do the work on their own. Carrying the three references costs about 1.3p a call in image input tokens, which takes a render from 0.96p to 2.3p — still cheaper than a GPT-Image-2 image, but two and a half times a plain Flare one.

05

Recommendation

Model

Move the diagram pipeline to gpt-image-2.5-flare at medium and change nothing else. It draws the same picture for a quarter of the tokens and a third of the wall-clock time, and the gain shows where the old canary hurt most: the map of German expansion that GPT-Image-2 failed three times before it was binned came back on the first attempt with its four arrows in the right order and the right places, one correction short of accepted rather than beyond saving. Lettering is now good rather than solved: over 40 images the round produced one non-word (“traceria” for trachea) and one doubled full stop, while German shop signs, note denominations, place names and four-figure percentages all came back clean. What still fails is spatial, not textual — leader lines land a few pixels into the neighbouring structure, which is precisely what a retry fixes. The house-style block, the landscape size, the brief agent and the gate all carry over untouched; the only edit is the model string. Sunburst earns its place only for reference work, and this round says that work is not yet worth buying.

Style

Keep A, the textbook block as the house style, and add B, line-and-wash as a second register the brief agent may choose for history and for anything with a human subject. The three blocks are separated by taste, not by pass rate — the gate accepted two A, two B and one C — so the argument is in what each one does when it goes wrong. B is the more beautiful and the one that matches the painted spines on the shelf; the hyperinflation scene and the Versailles map are the best pictures in this round. But it decorates: on the bar chart it bolted period vignettes onto the plot area, and washes soften exactly the fine distinctions a cell diagram lives on. C is not a house style. Flat isotype keeps reaching for faceless silhouettes, which is a rule already settled, and it drops the distinctions the label list exists to make — the animal cell lost its membrane, the map lost the meaning of its own colours.

References

Half a result, and the useful half is the surprising one. References carried the chrome cleanly across four unrelated subjects: the same paper, the same label face and size, the same thin leader ending in a small anchor dot, the same numbered accent disc, the same margins, the same restraint — the parts a written style block struggles to pin down. What they did not carry is the painting: fill and shading drifted to whatever each subject’s own convention wanted, so the waves came back as bare line art and the processor as flat pastel boxes. So references are worth using to hold one unit together, and worth stealing from for the next draft of the written block — but at roughly double the price per call they are not how to run a fleet, and Sunburst is not needed for the fleet at all.

Then

  1. Swap the model string in scripts/diagrams/canary_generate.py and re-run one canary unit end to end, retries and all, to measure the real per-accepted cost with the retry loop in.
  2. Add the two faults this round exposed to the gate’s standing checks: leader lines that land on the neighbouring structure, and free-floating prose blocks that are captions in all but name.
  3. Pilot on Unity’s 552 article lessons, then open the free tier.
  4. Re-test the Batch allow-list in a fortnight; the discount is worth a second look, not a wait.
